newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy opens interests section in Baghdad.
newsitem.headline: Italy opens interests section in Baghdad.

text.p: Italy confirmed on Wednesday that it was opening an interests section in Iraq, five years after Baghdad severed diplomatic ties.
A Foreign Ministry statement, issued in response to news agency reports from the Iraqi capital, said "Italy has opened its own interests section at the Hungarian Embassy in Baghdad".
It said the office would be headed by Cesare Ragaglini, a diplomat with the rank of counsellor. Ragaglini would pay a first visit to Baghdad next week, the statement said.
Iraq severed diplomatic ties with Italy and other Arab and Western countries which took part in the U.S.-led military coalition that drove Iraqi troops out of Kuwait in 1991.
Scores of Italian businessmen and traders have flocked to Baghdad recently to secure deals in the lucrative market. Italy was Iraq's fourth trading partner before the Gulf crisis.

Iraq is under stringent U.N. trade sanctions imposed on it after its 1990 invasion of Kuwait. The curbs include a ban on Iraq's oil exports and imports of all commodities except for food and medicine, for which Iraq has little cash to pay.

Antonio Loche, Secretary-General of the government-funded Italian Institute for Asia, said in Baghdad on Tuesday that an Iraqi diplomat had left for Rome on Monday to head Iraq's interest section, operating under the Sudanese flag.
